headline: Cybersecurity stocks fell sharply on Friday, with Palo Alto down 7%, SentinelOne down 9% and Zscaler down 6%, as worries about how AI spending is funded spread.
score_reason: Sector price move reported by one outlet; informative on how far the AI sell-off has spread, but a narrow slice of the market.
importance_line: Savers and traders holding security shares feel it first, then the security firms that may find fundraising harder, though the report ties the fall to AI financing worries even though the stocks also fell with the wider tech sell-off.
summary: 24/7 Wall St reports that in afternoon trading on Friday the cybersecurity firms Palo Alto Networks, SentinelOne and Zscaler fell 7%, 9% and 6%, and a fund tracking the sector dropped about 4%, more than double the 1.72% fall in the Nasdaq-100 tracker QQQ. The selling came even after Citi raised its price target on Palo Alto on Thursday, citing a survey of chief information officers that showed AI projects lifting security spending.
notes: Yahoo Finance carries this 24/7 Wall St article, so 24/7 Wall St is credited as the source; Yahoo link is where the text was read.
